function.name: calculate_investment_value
function.description: Calculate the future value of an investment given the principal, interest rate and term. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

principal.description: The initial amount of the investment. This is a float type value.

interest_rate.description: The annual interest rate in percentage. Enter as a decimal (for 5%, enter 0.05). This is a float type value.

term.description: The term of the investment in years.

compounding.description: The number of times that interest is compounded per year. Default is 1 (annually).

message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Director | Why it’s worth watching |
|------|-------|----------|------------------------|
| 1978 | **The Shining** | Stanley Kubrick | Masterful atmosphere, iconic performances, psychological dread. |
| 1980 | **The Thing** | John Carpenter | Tense paranoia, practical effects, unforgettable twist. |
| 1984 | **A Nightmare on Elm Street** | Wes Craven | Introduced Freddy Krueger, blending dream logic with slasher thrills. |
| 1999 | **The Sixth Sense** | M. Night Shyamalan | Suspenseful storytelling, a twist that redefined the genre. |
| 2002 | **28 Days Later** | Danny Boyle | Fast‑paced zombie outbreak, gritty realism, social commentary. |
| 2004 | **Saw** | James Wan & Leigh Whannell | Dark, inventive traps, moral dilemmas, cult‑status. |
| 2007 | **Paranormal Activity** | Oren Peli | Found‑footage style, subtle terror, huge box‑office success. |
| 2010 | **The Conjuring** | James Wan | Supernatural scares, strong character arcs, franchise launchpad. |
| 2012 | **The Cabin in the Woods** | Drew Goddard | Meta‑take on horror tropes, clever twists, fun for fans. |
| 2014 | **It Follows** | David Robert Mitchell | Unique premise, creeping dread, indie charm. |
| 2015 | **The Witch** | Robert Eggers | Period authenticity, slow‑burn tension, unsettling atmosphere. |
| 2017 | **Get Out** | Jordan Peele | Social satire meets horror, sharp commentary, critical acclaim. |
| 2018 | **Hereditary** | Ari Aster | Psychological horror, intense performances, disturbing imagery. |
| 2019 | **Midsommar** | Ari Aster | Daylight horror, unsettling rituals, striking visuals. |
| 2020 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Modern retelling, claustrophobic tension, feminist angle. |
| 2021 | **A Quiet Place Part II** | John Krasinski | Sound‑based suspense, emotional stakes, sequel payoff. |
| 2022 | **The Black Phone** | Scott Derrickson | Creepy telephones, supernatural mystery, strong pacing. |
| 2023 | **M3GAN** | Gerard Johnstone | AI horror, uncanny doll, contemporary fears. |
| 2024 | **The Last Voyage of the Demeter** | Christopher R. Gattuso | Lovecraftian lore, atmospheric dread, fresh take on Dracula myth. |

Feel free to pick based on your preferred sub‑genre—psychological, supernatural, slasher, or found‑footage—and enjoy the chills!
